# wsjtx

**Weak-signal digital modes — FT8, FT4, JT65, JT9, WSPR, Q65**

- **Version recorded:** 3.0.2
- **Categories:** `digital-modes`
- **Upstream:** <https://wsjtx.github.io/wsjtx/index.html>
- **Needs first:** `libhamlib4t64`

## What it does

Decodes and transmits the weak-signal modes that dominate modern HF digital operating, principally FT8 and FT4, plus WSPR for propagation beaconing and Q65 for weak-signal VHF and EME work.

## Why you would want it

FT8 is the most-used mode on HF, and this is the reference implementation. It makes contacts possible on bands and at power levels where nothing else gets through. **This is the catalog's recommended default of the FT8 family** (maintainer ruling, 2026-08-30): every guide and third-party document assumes it, and it is packaged on every target. The forks stay carried — wsjtx-improved for marginal-decode tuning, jtdx and mshv for their own followings — and js8call is a different mode, not an alternative.

## Before it will work

Accurate system clock (within about a second), CAT rig control, and audio routed both ways between radio and computer.

## How it installs

- git (cmake) — https://github.com/WSJTX/wsjtx at `v3.0.2`
  - build dependencies: `gfortran`, `libboost-dev`, `libboost-log-dev`, `libboost-filesystem-dev`, `qttools5-dev`, `qttools5-dev-tools`, `qtmultimedia5-dev`, `libqt5serialport5-dev`, `libfftw3-dev`, `libreadline-dev`, `libusb-1.0-0-dev`, `libudev-dev`, `libhamlib-dev`

Binaries this produces:

- `wsjtx`

This displaces the distribution's own `wsjtx` (**D-022**: coexist, disclose, never remove silently).

## Known problems

Under Wayland on Raspberry Pi the window renders without borders or decorations; switch to X11. That report is inherited from AHRL's operational notes and has not been reproduced here — no Pi has run this build yet. The repository package is purged first because the source build uses the same prefix.

## Toolkit risk

- `qt5`: in progress, checked 2026-08-25 — qttools5, qtmultimedia5, libqt5serialport5. Qt6 port under way upstream.
